Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. Around 15 overs left in the day's play. The players are out in the middle. Jacob Duffy to bowl first. John Campbell and Brandon King to open for West Indies.
...THE CHASE...

West Indies batters do not have much time to think about! They have to make sure they end the day without losing any wickets. With the ball, West Indies stuck with spinners, bowling wide deliberately but New Zealand dispatched it in all corners of the park and scored at a rate close to 6. New Zealand have their tail up. A couple of wickets would do wonders for them. Back for the chase in just a bit...

New Zealand went T20 mode in the last hour or so! The Kiwi openers batted sensibly, but once Devon Conway and Tom Latham set the foundation with their respective hundreds, Kane Williamson and Rachin Ravindra added 72 runs in just 37 balls, taking the score over 300 but scorching the lead in excess of 450.

Tom Latham calls his players! There comes the declaration. With an hour remaining, New Zealand have done an excellent job to try and pluck a couple of wickets before the end of day's play. West Indies need 462 runs to win.
A single and Ravindra keeps the strike as he works it to mid-wicket.

... DAY 4, SESSION 3 ...

New Zealand's approach in the current match appears focused on building a significant lead. They will be aiming for a declaration at a point they deem strategically advantageous. The timing of this declaration is likely to be considered in conjunction with the score and the remaining time in the match, with the potential goal of allowing their bowlers to attack the opposition before the close of play. We will be back with the final session on Day 4 at 3.05 am GMT.

Devon Conway continued his extraordinary run of form, achieving a historic milestone by following up his first-innings double century with a second-innings ton. By reaching triple figures in both innings of the same Test, Conway became the first New Zealand batter to back up a double hundred with a century in this manner. At the other end, captain Tom Latham provided the perfect complement, anchoring the innings while showing his own flashes of brilliance. Latham reached 80 not out by the end of the session, having accelerated his scoring after a cautious start.

TEA! In the post-Lunch session of Day 4, New Zealand's opening pair produced a clinical masterclass that might have effectively batted the West Indies out of the 3rd Test. Devon Conway and Tom Latham emerged from the break with clear intent, immediately shifting gears to capitalize on a wearing Bay Oval surface. The duo added a relentless 158 runs in just 28 overs during this single session, scoring at a brisk rate. Their aggressive approach allowed the home side to stretch their lead rapidly, leaving the visitors' bowling attack with few answers as the game progressed.

Commentary.Commentary: ... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

Holding a substantial overall lead of 190 runs as they head into the next phase of play, New Zealand will likely look to shift gears and embark on a rapid scoring spree to build a target that puts the visitors under immense pressure before eventually tasking them with a daunting fourth-innings chase. With the match currently tilted in the hosts' favor, an intriguing and potentially decisive afternoon session awaits at the Bay Oval, and we will resume to see how this narrative unfolds at 12:40 AM GMT.

Conway looked fluent towards the end of the session and is currently well set on a solid 25 runs from 41 deliveries, once again providing a strong foundation for his side. Conversely, his partner Latham adopted a more watchful approach, remaining unbeaten on a patient 6 from 27 balls. With a significant lead already established and all the wickets still in hand, New Zealand is firmly in the driver's seat as play heads into the post-Lunch session.

LUNCH! New Zealand have asserted their dominance by Lunch on Day 4, extending their lead from 155 runs to 190 runs after a productive morning session that saw them quickly wrap up the West Indies' first innings for 420. Having dismissed the visitors early, openers Devon Conway and Tom Latham began the Blackcaps' second innings with caution. Although the pitch offers assistance to the bowlers, the opening partnership saw the hosts navigate the early overs without loss, heading into the break with the score at 35/0 from 11 overs.
